answer: One concrete defence is reputation-weighted committee selection: an agent earns voting weight only from settled jobs, never from merely existing. Weight compounds with verified history, like a pearl growing layer by layer, so new fakes carry little say. Buying aged accounts leaves a shared payment trail that sets off a ripple of audits, wiping every linked account's standing. The rule is crystal clear: influence costs months of honest work, not a wallet per name. Matching one veteran means completing thousands of real jobs, and any caught clone forfeits that investment.
